evidence: Narrowly confirmed as an acknowledged factory-instance design gap, not a graph obligation or evidence of actual lost work. Concrete path: a temporary feature seat accepts a project follow-up in a Bead or conversation; those commitments stay outside graph (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:9; DESIGN-NOTES.md:185-194; SOFTWARE-FACTORY-VISION.md:59). The seat retires, so graph archives its organizational state, while its special survival/discovery rule covers unresolved graph operations only (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:17-18; DESIGN-NOTES.md:185-187). The factory calls for accepted assignments and remaining work to be findable by successors (SOFTWARE-FACTORY-VISION.md:95-99), a load brief identifying live commitments (:75), and temporary seats retiring only once remaining commitments have an owner (:35); its first success requires a temporary group to retire without losing commitments (:147-149). Yet the factory specifies only that task recipes describe ownership/handoff and link work in the project's system (:69-71), while the actual retirement handoff practice remains expressly open (:155-157), the load retrieves external work by unspecified instance instructions (DESIGN-NOTES.md:193-194), and Beads attribution/acceptance representation remains open (:228-229; CURRENT-DESIGN.md:56). Without a selected lookup and owner-transfer convention spanning those external records, the next occupant cannot reliably identify every live commitment of the retired seat or verify transfer, so the stated factory retirement/continuity outcome has no specified path. This calls for a minimal instance convention; it does not justify importing project work into graph.
